Second, Jio.

And third, Reliance Retail.

So if you ask me what really surprised the market, it was extraordinary performance of

Let's first understand the basic economics.
Reliance has one of the world's largest integrated refining and petrochemical complexes.
The company buys crude oil basically and processes it in the refineries and converts it into
various products, petrol, diesel, aviation fuel and other petroleum products.
It also manufactures petroleum products that eventually go into plastics, polyester and
several other industries.
Now imagine a situation where the global supply of these products suddenly becomes constrained.
Demand is still there but availability of this in the supply side is reducing.
What happens to the selling price of those products?
It can increase significantly and that is broadly what happened during this quarter.
Because of the geopolitical disruption in the Middle East and Russia, several refining
operations were affected completely like there were some bombs that was going into Russian
refineries including that.
The movement of crude oil and the finished products was also disrupted.
Inventories of important petroleum products came down drastically and global refining
margin started expanding dramatically because of this demand and supply mismatch.
Reliance management said gasoline cracks were approximately three times higher than the
previous year, diesel cracks were around 3.5 times higher and aviation fuel cracks were
approximately 3.7 times higher.
Let me explain what a crack spread means.
Suppose a refinery purchases crude oil and converts it into a petrol or diesel.
The difference between the selling value of the finished product and the cost of crude
is broadly called as crack spread.
This is not the final profit of the refinery because you still have operating cost, transportation
and energy cost and other expenses that put together gives some other expense also for
the refinery.
But still when the difference increases substantially the refinery has an opportunity to make significant
more money than what it actually made previously and Reliance was in the position to capture
that opportunity.
But wait, there is something more interesting than this.
